rules.action: Wire both branches before stenting. Use jailed SB wire technique for the provisional approach.
rules.rationale: Jailed SB wire protects against abrupt SB closure and facilitates re-access without significantly increasing complexity.
rules.detail: For SB <2mm, jailing is optional. Confirm SB wire position in the distal SB with contrast before MV stenting.

rules.action: Provisional single-stent strategy is the default for all bifurcation lesions.
rules.rationale: Provisional is non-inferior to upfront 2-stent for most anatomies with lower contrast load, radiation, and stent burden per EBC/ESC consensus.
rules.detail: Upfront 2-stent is indicated only when SB >2.5mm AND Medina SB segment = 1 (true ostial SB disease). Do not default to 2-stent for large SB without ostial disease.

rules.action: POT is mandatory immediately after MV stent deployment.
rules.rationale: POT opens the struts, reduces SB pinching, and facilitates SB rewiring through the proximal cell. rePOT after any SB balloon inflation restores MV stent geometry.
rules.detail: Short NC balloon sized to the proximal MV reference diameter, inflated at the proximal stent edge with the carina as the distal marker. rePOT mandatory after any SB balloon inflation.

rules.action: Re-wire SB through the proximal stent cell after MV stent deployment.
rules.rationale: Proximal cell rewiring ensures optimal strut configuration and reduces strut distortion on KBI.
rules.detail: Confirm wire position in the distal SB with contrast before balloon inflation. Inadvertent distal cell entry compromises strut reconstruction.

rules.action: KBI indicated only if: SB TIMI <3, residual SB ostial stenosis >75%, or significant SB ostial dissection.
rules.rationale: Routine KBI in provisional PCI does not improve outcomes in unselected cases and increases complexity.
rules.detail: KBI for these specific rescue indications remains appropriate. Routine KBI without these indications should be avoided.
rules.caution: Do not perform routine KBI — reserved for the indications above only.

rules.action: Upfront 2-stent technique is indicated. FKBI is mandatory after all 2-stent techniques.
rules.rationale: Large SB (>2.5mm) with true ostial SB disease (Medina SB=1) is an established upfront 2-stent indication per EBC/ESC consensus.
rules.detail: DK-Crush preferred for most anatomies based on DKCRUSH-V data. Culotte preferred when both branches are of similar calibre and angle is non-acute. FKBI failure is associated with significantly higher MACE.

rules.action: FKBI (final kissing balloon inflation) is mandatory after all 2-stent techniques.
rules.rationale: Failure to perform FKBI after 2-stent techniques is associated with significantly higher MACE.
rules.detail: Both balloons must be inflated simultaneously. Ensure simultaneous marker alignment at the carina.

rules.action: DK-Crush strongly favoured over Culotte for acute SB take-off angle (<45°).
rules.rationale: T-shaped anatomy makes rewiring through crushed struts more predictable with DK-Crush. Culotte is technically challenging with acute-angle bifurcations due to difficult wire manipulation.
rules.detail: After crushing, re-wiring through the proximal cell is critical. Inadvertent distal cell entry compromises the first kissing balloon and SB ostial reconstruction.

rules.action: Culotte is a favourable technique for obtuse/wide SB take-off angle (>70°), particularly when both branches are of similar calibre.
rules.rationale: Wide angle facilitates rewiring and full strut coverage of both ostia in Culotte. DK-Crush remains an acceptable alternative with comparable long-term outcomes.
rules.detail: FKBI is mandatory regardless of technique.
